text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
NASA BORBA
- Serbian parliament speaker and acting president Dragan Tomic invites OSCE observers for Serbia's presidential and parliamentary elections set for September 21.

- Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) delegation in Montenegro at invitation of Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic. Ruling Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) of Montenegro President Milica Pejanovic-Djurisic says SPS will probably nominate Bulatovic as its candidate for Montenegrin president.
- SPS election campaign starts in Serbia.
- Serbian Renewal Movement (SPO) says it will decide on participation in Serbia elections by August 12.

- The phenomenon of (Serbian Radical Party leader Vojislav) Seselj is not the ugly but the real face of the national intelligence's programme, says the Social Democratic Union's Zarko Korac on attacks by radicals on non-Serbs in Serbia.
- Production in Yugoslavia rising statistically, but not the GDP, says Economics Institute analyst Miroljub Labus.
- The Federal Customs Office has over the past two and a half years failed to transfer nearly one billion dinars to federal and republican budgets, a central bank report said.
- Zastava arms workers of Kragujevac announce protests in Belgrade over deteriorating situation in the factory.
- "I don't know whether I am under investigation," says Moslem National Council of Sandzak leader Sulejman Ugljanin ahead of hearing in Novi Pazar district court set for July 30.
- Closing down of radio and TV stations in Serbia halted until elections, says Yugoslav Telecommunications Minister Dojcilo Radojevic.
POLITIKA
- Yugoslav-Macedonian trade should reach $520 million this year, up $100 million on 1996, said Dose Kotevski, director of the Chamber of Commerce of Macedonia in Belgrade.

- Serbian government has secured 45 million German marks for buy up of export-oriented production of fruits and 75 million marks for purchase of 40 percent of the value of 600 tonnes of '97 wheat crop, said minister coordinator in the Serbian government Dragan Tomic.
- Serbian privatisation minister Milan Beko said the Serbian Development Fund have already allocated some 600 million German marks for export-oriented production.
BORBA

- Serbian Agriculture Minister Jovan Babovic said harvest completed on 70 percent of some 812,000 hectares under wheat with an average yield 3.8 tonnes per hectare. Serbia this year expects 180 million marks from fruit exports, to invest some 100 million for production of agricultural machinery and 50 million marks in cattle breeding, Babovic said.
- ICN Pharmaceuticals Inc. and Macedonian Ohis signed an agreement over the week-end on founding ICN Makedonija.

- Serbian petrochemical complex Petrohemija of Pancevo director Slobodan Tresac said January-June exports were worth $70 million, which means the plant could exceed by $20 million its annual export plan set at $130 million.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Smederevo region suffers biggest flood damages so far. Several thousand flats flooded and many villages left without electricity. A dozen factories, firms and warehouses damaged.

- French car maker Peugeot seen as a new partner to Kragujevac-based Zastava car manufacturer. Zastava General Manager Srboljub Vasovic declined to comment and insisted Zastava also negotiated with Hyundai, Renault, VW and Fiat.
- Heavy rains in northern Serbia seen favourable for maize, sugar beet, sunflower and other crops.
- At least 2,000 signatures needed for a presidential candidate in Montenegro for presidential elections due October 5. Montenegrin president is elected for a five-year term.
GRADJANIN

- Belgrade hotels work at 25-30 percent capacity. Belgrade Tourist Association Director Bojan Zecevic cites bad political image and inadequate offer as key reasons behind record low numbers of foreign tourists.
DNEVNI TELEGRAF

- Greek, Italian, French and British investors most interested in concessions for building Nis-Dimitrovgrad, Leskovac-Macedonian border, Belgrade-Subotica sections of highway, says Serbian Transport and Telecommunications Minister Svetolik Kostadinovic.
BLIC
- Serbian ethnic Albanians will not participate in upcoming presidental and parliamentary elections, said ethnic Albanian lawyer Azem Vlasi, former communist Kosovo leader.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --
POBJEDA

- One of the reasons for the visit of the SPS delegation to Podgorica could be to give support to its candidate for the forthcoming presidential elections in Montenegro, which could bring into question future cooperation between SPS and the DPS, says Svetozar Marovic, DPS vice president.
- "Conflicts in DPS could have been avoided. Unfortunately I did not meet with President Bulatovic's understanding for such an approach," says Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic.

- Civic Resistance Movement organises protest outside Montenegrin presidency against visit by senior SPS delegation to Bulatovic. "Citizens of Montengro, let us help Momir Bulatovic understand that he is political past in Montenegro and Slobodan Milosevic that Montenegro is not for sale," the movement said in a statement. -- Belgrade newsroom + 381 11 311 4305
